1.

Heard Sri Prem Prakash Yadav, learned counsel for the revisionist and Sri R.K.Verma, learned
A.G.A. for the State.

2. This criminal revision has been filed by the revisionist for setting aside the impugned order dated
26.10.2023 passed by Special Judge (Pocso Act, Azamgarh in Special Case No.61 of 2021, State vs.
Jittu @ Jitendra, under Sections 363, 302, 201 7 376 (3) I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Pocso Act, P.S.
Saraimeer, District Azamgarh whereby application moved under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for summoning
and recall for examination of a witness was rejected.

4.  Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that an application from the side of the revisionist under Section 311 Cr.P.C. has been moved with a prayer to summon the expert from forensic laboratory to prove D.N.A. test report, but the same has been rejected by the trial court.

sentences.text:
Contention of the revisionist is that examination of the witnesses is necessary for the just decision in the case, therefore, the impugned order may be set aside and court may be directed to summon the witness.
6. Submission of the revisionist is opposed by learned A.G.A.
7.
The application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. was moved on 20.09.2023 before the trial court.
This is three line application which is reproduced as below:
8. Admittedly this application has been moved at the stage when the statements under Section 313 Cr.P.C. had already been recorded.

9. Section 311 Cr.P.C. is as below:-
"311. Power to summon material witness, or examine person present.

- Any Court may, at any stage of any inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code, summon any person in attendance, though not summoned as a witness, or recall and re-examine any person already examined; and the Court shall summon and examine or recall and re-examine any such person if his evidence appears to it to be essential to the just decision of the case."
10.
Under the provisions of section 311 Cr.P.C., the court has a plenary power to summon any person at any stage of the proceedings as a witness.
This power includes recall and re-examination of any person who has already been examined.
This power is to be exercised when the court finds it necessary to summon/recall any witness for just decision of the case.
The law puts no fetters on the powers of the courts to call for any witness to attain the highest goal of justice.

In my opinion this provision of law gives expression to the inherent power of the courts which is available to them by virtue of being the supreme authority who has been entrusted with responsibility to do justice.
The power lies with the Court alone as juxtaposed to rights or powers of parties.

The others stake holders whether prosecution or defence, have a limited role of drawing the attention of the court and putting the relevant material before it which may assist it in arriving at a correct inference.

sentences.text: In my view, because the revisionist did not elaborate how the examination of the scientific expert is necessary for just decision of the case and further has not been able to show any good ground for such summoning in this revision as well, the order passed by the trial court is not liable for interference by this Court.
It is further noted that genuineness of the document has already been accepted by the defence and in such circumstances such document is readable in evidence under Section 294 Cr.P.C..
Further document being a report of scientific expert, the scientific expert need not be called by the court in a routine manner.
Section 293 Cr.P.C. provides that any document purporting to be a report under the hand of government scientific expert may be used as evidence in the enquiry and trial without any formal proof.
12. In view of the above, I do not find merit in this revision.
Hence, the criminal revision is dismissed.
Order Date :- 15.3.2024
